incidents.victim: Tor network users
incidents.vector: An unidentified actor compromised more than 330 Tor relay servers, infected them with Ebury Linux malware, and converted them into exit relays to intercept SSH connections and downgrade/sniff unencrypted email traffic.
incidents.impact: More than 10% of Tor exit relays were affected before detection; the Tor security team blocklisted compromised servers in one of the largest security incidents in Tor's history.

incidents.victim: Burger King Japan
incidents.vector: Attackers accessed a server managing the company's smartphone app.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 11.18 million users, including names, dates of birth, email addresses, phone numbers, and gender, was stolen.

incidents.victim: Staples
incidents.vector: A Chinese organized crime group gained access to an internal Staples application ('Nexus') and used it to issue fraudulent gift cards.
incidents.impact: Attackers issued more than 15,000 gift cards worth over $5 million for retailers including Target and Sephora, using them to buy electronics shipped to China for resale.

incidents.victim: Zeabur
incidents.vector: A hacker stole environment variables and other account records in the company's second breach of the year, following an August incident involving its AWS backend.
incidents.impact: Records for more than 320,000 accounts, including environment variables, were stolen; the company will shut down entirely at year's end.

incidents.victim: At least 20 Japanese companies and South Korean banks/financial institutions
incidents.vector: An unidentified threat actor used a Chinese AI agent named Artex to conduct automated intrusions.
incidents.impact: At least 20 Japanese companies were hacked, with the same AI agent also used in intrusions against South Korean banks and financial institutions earlier in the month.

incidents.victim: ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers (MSPs and downstream tenants)
incidents.vector: A threat actor obtained a sensitive API secret for ConnectWise's Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) application and used it to authenticate directly into customers' Microsoft 365 tenants, bypassing MFA.
incidents.impact: Huntress confirmed unauthorized sign-ins across 162 tenants out of nearly 1,000 targeted, with attackers elevating privileges to Global Administrator and planting backup credentials in at least two tenants; ConnectWise disabled Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management pending investigation.

incidents.victim: John Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins, and 100+ other e-commerce sites
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking threat actor used the AI-driven penetration-testing tool Cairn to automate discovery of SQL injection, insecure deserialization, and authentication-bypass flaws, then deployed web shells for persistent access.
incidents.impact: More than 100 global e-commerce and payment sites were compromised; a web shell was confirmed installed on at least one commercial site, with separate operations targeting credit-card data and cryptocurrency.

incidents.victim: Naval shipbuilder, aircraft engine manufacturer, and law enforcement agency (two NATO countries, unnamed)
incidents.vector: Attackers gained initial access via a malicious Microsoft Word attachment, then deployed the Hookedge backdoor and an in-memory code-execution tool to steal credentials and reconnaissance data.
incidents.impact: Hackers maintained access to defense-related networks for at least two months; researchers could not confirm whether sensitive data was exfiltrated, but assess defense-related information was the likely objective.

incidents.victim: AOMEI Backupper customers (IT services, telecom, higher education)
incidents.vector: Attackers repeatedly tampered with AOMEI's update-server configuration files in short 5-10 minute bursts between April and July 2026, redirecting the backup software's update channel to deliver the CROSSROAD downloader and SHINYROAD backdoor.
incidents.impact: Victims across IT services, telecommunications, and higher education in nearly a dozen countries, including the US, Australia, India, and Brazil, were infected; AOMEI has not yet identified or notified all affected customers.

incidents.victim: Intermarché, Carrefour, Monoprix, Leclerc, Coopérative U (French supermarket chains)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised internet-exposed remote controllers (Danfoss AK-SM/AK-SC, Copeland xweb, Dixell xweb) on end-of-life commercial refrigeration systems, forcing units into a continuous 50°C defrost cycle.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of French supermarkets had refrigeration systems disrupted, with losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros from spoiled food stock; French prosecutors estimate roughly 700 victims.

incidents.victim: California Department of Education (via contractor Educational Testing Service)
incidents.vector: Attackers used a compromised account to repeatedly access contractor ETS's secure file-transfer site between May 22 and September 18, 2026.
incidents.impact: Personal, demographic, disability, and standardized-testing data covering all California public school students enrolled since 2006 (roughly 7 million students) was copied; no evidence of public disclosure has been found to date.

incidents.victim: AI policy experts at US think tanks, universities, and law firms
incidents.vector: Attackers impersonated former US officials to build rapport, then sent adversary-in-the-middle phishing links using a customized browser-in-the-browser tool to steal OneDrive credentials and session tokens, bypassing MFA.
incidents.impact: Targets at US- and Japan-based think tanks, universities, and law firms had cloud account credentials and authenticated sessions compromised, supporting Chinese intelligence-gathering on US AI policy.

incidents.victim: H2O Retailing (Hankyu Hanshin department stores)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a website operated by the company's Hankyu Hanshin department store brand.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to 1.26 million customers was stolen.

incidents.victim: Alternative for Germany (AfD) political party
incidents.vector: A hacker obtained data from the party's web hosting provider.
incidents.impact: 281GB of internal data, including email inboxes, website databases, and internal documents, was leaked publicly.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, government, and other sectors
incidents.vector: Ransomware affiliates exploited an authentication-bypass vulnerability in PAN-OS GlobalProtect portals/gateways to establish VPN sessions, bypass MFA, and pivot directly to virtualization infrastructure (vCenter/ESXi) for domain-wide credential theft.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation since early June 2026 has affected organizations across at least 11 industry sectors, with ransomware operators using the access to stage data exfiltration and ransomware deployment.

incidents.victim: University of Belgrade rector and a Serbian prosecutor
incidents.vector: A zero-click exploit requiring no user interaction infected devices with NSO Group's Pegasus spyware.
incidents.impact: Confirmed infection of the University of Belgrade rector, a prominent protest-movement figure, and a prosecutor investigating a Trump-linked Belgrade development deal, ahead of Serbia's October 25 parliamentary elections.

incidents.victim: U.S. federal bankruptcy court system (Bankruptcy Noticing Center)
incidents.vector: Not disclosed; the attack disrupted the Bankruptcy Noticing Center, a platform managed by contractor BAE Systems.
incidents.impact: The BNC and other BAE-managed court websites were taken offline, disrupting notices for federal bankruptcy cases nationwide.

incidents.victim: Nikkei
incidents.vector: Hackers used stolen credentials to access a cloud server.
incidents.impact: 1.83 million records were stolen in the company's third security breach in the past month.

incidents.victim: Government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure (unspecified)
incidents.vector: Attackers deployed AI-generated web shells, a custom Go-based RAT (SysGoRAT), and in-memory reverse shells against Linux servers, exfiltrating databases and government mailboxes while using anti-forensic techniques, including planted fake red-team markers.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed persistent access and data exfiltration attempts against government Linux infrastructure from October 2025 through April 2026, with multiple payloads containing AI-generated code comments indicating automated or AI-assisted development.

incidents.victim: US government, critical manufacturing, healthcare, and IT organizations (multiple victims)
incidents.vector: A China-based company, Integrity Technology Group, provided botnet infrastructure, VPN services, and penetration-testing tools (including a custom scanner called MicroScan) that enabled Chinese state-linked actors to exploit networks via credential theft, XSS attacks, and password-spraying tools.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA, NSA, and allied agencies issued a joint advisory describing exploitation of US and foreign networks across government, critical manufacturing, healthcare, IT, law enforcement, education, and religious sectors since at least 2021.
